title: Moonshot Said to Eye Early 2027 IPO After Value Hits $50 Billion
source_used: The Japan Times (https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2026/10/06/moonshot-ai-ipo-plans/) and The Business Times, both carrying Bloomberg's article text; The Standard (HK) summary. Bloomberg page itself blocked (HTTP 403).
key_facts: Bloomberg reported on 6 Oct 2026, citing people familiar, that Moonshot AI has closed the final round of private fundraising at a valuation of about $50 billion and is heading toward a Hong Kong IPO in the first quarter of 2027.
It has begun laying groundwork for early-look meetings to gauge investor sentiment, starting as soon as October, and is considering raising up to $5 billion.
A previous round this summer valued Moonshot at $31.5 billion.
Annual recurring revenue is expected to rise to $2 billion by December from $1 billion now, people familiar said; it was $300 million in June, Bloomberg reported earlier.
Bank of America is overall coordinator; sponsor banks are China International Capital, Deutsche Bank and Goldman Sachs; the company has filed confidentially.
It is unclear how the valuation or IPO timeline may be affected by tighter oversight after regulators opened a data-security probe into DeepSeek and Moonshot, according to The Information.
Deliberations are ongoing and the IPO timing might still change; Moonshot did not respond to requests for comment during a Chinese public holiday.
Moonshot is a Beijing-based AI lab founded in early 2023 by Yang Zhilin; backers include Alibaba, Tencent and 5Y Capital; its Kimi K3 open model debuted in July.
quote_evidence: Moonshot AI has closed the final round of private fundraising at a valuation of about $50 billion and is heading toward an initial public offering in Hong Kong in the first quarter of next year, according to people familiar with the matter.
Deliberations are ongoing and the timing of the IPO might still change, the people said.

It is unclear how the valuation or the IPO timeline may be affected by tighter oversight of China’s AI industry after regulators opened a data-security probe into DeepSeek and Moonshot, according to The Information, adding to broader concerns over governance and safety.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading Chinese AI lab has fixed a $50 billion valuation and is lining up a Hong Kong listing, though a reported regulatory probe could affect timing.
notes: Bloomberg's page could not be opened; the full Bloomberg text was read on The Japan Times and The Business Times (BLOOMBERG credit). The Information's probe report was not read; it is cited only as Bloomberg relays it.
